note: Attacker-controlled bytes enter the fuzzer as an IPv6 message payload; first byte controls link security, rest is the IPv6 packet.
First validation loop reads each TLV header from the CoAP payload; tlv.GetLength() is attacker-controlled and must be <= Dataset::kMaxValueSize (16).
ActiveTimestampTlv is read from the message; its length field is attacker-controlled but bounded by sizeof(ActiveTimestampTlv)=10 during the read.
MeshLocalPrefixTlv is read from the message; Tlv::Get reads sizeof(MeshLocalPrefixTlv)=10 bytes into the stack buffer, but the TLV's length field retains the attacker-controlled value (15).
IsValid() only checks GetLength() >= 8; it does not enforce an upper bound, so a length of 15 passes validation.

memcmp reads meshLocalPrefix.GetLength()=15 bytes from meshLocalPrefix.GetMeshLocalPrefix(), which is only uint8_t[8]; this reads 7 bytes past the stack buffer, causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ 15.
